children: Kiniksa Pharmaceuticals International reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $285.97 million, up 58.1% from a year earlier, while net income increased to $47.35 million and diluted EPS rose to $0.56. Growth was driven primarily by more patients receiving ARCALYST.
¹ Reported as “Total revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income”. ³ Reported as “income per share attributable to ordinary shareholders—diluted”.
ARCALYST net product revenue rose 58% year over year, primarily reflecting an increase in patients on therapy.
The pivotal Phase 3 PASTORALE trial of KPL-387 began enrolling and dosing. The company expects results in the second half of 2027.
A Phase 2 study is evaluating a transition to KPL-387 monotherapy, and a Phase 1 trial of KPL-1161 is expected to start by year-end 2026.
The FDA approved Samsung Biologics as ARCALYST’s replacement manufacturing partner in June 2026.
Higher sales and marketing spending reflected expanded promotional activity, including a direct-to-consumer campaign.
